grammar.title: What's outside a group with 以外
grammar.explanation: 以外 (yǐwài) means "apart from, besides, outside of" attached after a noun. Without 除了 in front, it often pairs with 都 or 也 to say what else is true beyond that one exception.

grammar.title: Describing fun with 有意思
grammar.explanation: 有意思 (yǒu yìsi) means "interesting, fun" describing something engaging. Its opposite is 没有意思 or 没意思 (boring).

sentences.pinyin: Zhè běn shū hěn yǒu yìsi.

sentences.zh: 他觉得这份工作很有意思。
sentences.pinyin: Tā juéde zhè fèn gōngzuò hěn yǒu yìsi.
sentences.en: He thinks this job is interesting.

sentences.pinyin: Tā yǐwài, dàjiā dōu lái le.

sentences.zh: 这个以外，你还要买什么？
sentences.pinyin: Zhège yǐwài, nǐ hái yào mǎi shénme?
sentences.en: Apart from this, what else do you want to buy?

sentences.zh: 中文以外，他还会说英语。
sentences.pinyin: Zhōngwén yǐwài, tā hái huì shuō Yīngyǔ.
sentences.en: Apart from Chinese, he can also speak English.

sentences.zh: 工作以外，他也喜欢运动。
sentences.pinyin: Gōngzuò yǐwài, tā yě xǐhuan yùndòng.
sentences.en: Apart from work, he also likes sports.

sentences.pinyin: Zhè běn shū yuè kàn yuè yǒuyìsi.
sentences.en: This book gets more interesting the more you read it.

sentences.zh: 我昨天买的书很有意思。
sentences.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān mǎi de shū hěn yǒuyìsi.
sentences.en: The book I bought yesterday is very interesting.
